title: Galley: unified intake, normalization, and certification flow for community model weights
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Goal: Build a single end-to-end flow (internal codename 'Galley') that automates community weight intake, canonical normalization, lightweight compatibility checks, and the creation of a verified performance profile that can be pinned for serving. This ticket covers the orchestration layer, conversion container integration, smoke validation harness, and telemetry/tracepoints needed for post-admit observability.

Scope: weights upload (signed manifests), deterministic conversion (fn/format normalization + dtype/shape checks), lightweight runtime compatibility checks (kernel/quantization hints), automated smoke generation (latency/cost/sample-quality), and publishing a profile artifact (pin + profile JSON + telemetry snapshot). Not included: heavy benchmarking job queue (handled by follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Uploader produces a signed manifest blob accepted by Galley and stored in artifact-bucket with a unique artifact_id
Conversion container executes deterministically for 95% of community weights seen in sample, producing canonical artifacts and artifacts metadata
Compatibility check returns kernel/quantization hints and a binary-pass/fail flag; failures emit actionable telemetry and a human review ticket
Smoke validation completes within configured budget (<= 5 minutes wall time) and publishes latency, peak-memory, and two sample generations to the profile store
Profile publish operation creates a pin schema object and writes to model-catalog with a documented version string and compatibility tags
steps: Design ingest API and signed-manifest schema (S3 presign + JWT signer)
Wire conversion container via conveyor worker; surface deterministic logs and provenance headers
Implement lightweight runtime probe that spins up a minimal runtime with kernel selection traces
Add a smoke harness with representative prompts and basic regression checks (toxicity/format/length)
Add telemetry points: ingest.latency, convert.duration, smoke.latency.p95, compatibility.fail_reasons
Publish profile artifact and trigger downstream indexing and console ingestion
comments: 2025-02-13 - Ava Kim: Kickoff meeting notes added; agreed to ship an MVP that flags failures for human review rather than auto-blocking. Action: Rohan to prototype conversion container interface.

2025-02-20 - Rohan Patel: Spike complete; conversion container contract requires explicit provenance headers and deterministic ordering of weight slices. Found three community tar formats that need un-tarring logic (tar, tar.zst, zip).
2025-02-24 - Priya Menon (SE): Reviewed smoke prompts and suggested adding an identity-preserving test for decoding differences between float16 and int8-quantized runs.
2025-02-27 - Security Review (initial): SSO service account pattern accepted; must add KMS-encrypted signing keys for manifests before release. Follow-up security ticket recommended.

2025-03-02 - Rohan Patel: Integration PR opened for conveyor worker and conversion container (github.com/redwood/conveyor/pull/778). Observed nondeterministic tensor ordering on two OSS models; mitigated with canonical sort by layer name.
2025-03-04 - QA: Smoke harness executed against 7 sample weights; 5 passed, 2 produced tokenizer mismatch errors — created ENG-61223 for tokenizer normalization work.
2025-03-05 - Ava Kim: Decision log: MVP will publish a 'quarantine' tag for artifacts failing compatibility instead of dropping them. This preserves lineage and allows manual triage.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Non-deterministic conversions can lead to flakey profiles and wrong pins. Mitigation: force canonical ordering, embed conversion checksums, and keep conversion logs as first-class telemetry so we can roll back pin if checksum mismatches observed in production. Also limit MVP to models smaller than 30B until heavy benchmarking pipeline is reachable.
release_notes_draft: Adds Galley onboarding flow: signed-manifest ingest, deterministic conversion container, lightweight runtime compatibility probe, and smoke validation that publishes an initial performance profile and pin. Quarantined models are tagged and require manual triage. Initial release scoped to community models <30B.
implementation_notes: Use conveyor v2 worker queue with concurrency=3 for conversion to limit resource contention. Conversion container should mount ephemeral NVMe for scratch. Instrument with trace_id propagated from ingest -> convert -> smoke -> publish. Profile JSON must include tokenization hash, conversion_checksum, p95 latency (short/long), peak_memory_mb, and a small sample generation list.
next_steps: Complete KMS signing integration and update ingest API
Run extended smoke on additional 25 community weights and iterate on failure handling
Schedule a design review for release gating and RBAC for manual triage UI
